questions.question: Why does the passage state that the number of precalculated values is O(nlogn)?

Because there are O(logn) range lengths that are powers of two.
Because the array size n multiplied by the query count gives O(nlogn).
Because the recursive formula requires O(logn) steps per element.

questions.explanation: The passage explicitly explains that the O(nlogn) bound comes from having O(logn) possible range lengths that are powers of two, leading to that many precalculated values per element.
